title: Condensed tame-inertia cohomology of finite-field representations with norm-topological coefficients
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. Fix a finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$, let $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ on profinite sets, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]; put $C_{F,T}=p_T^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories and direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

For a nonnegative integer $r$, let
$$G=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^r=H\times\mathbf Z_\ell^r,\qquad H=(\prod_{q\ne p,\ell}\mathbf Z_q)^r,$$
with the product profinite topology; $q$ ranges over primes and $\mathbf Z_q=\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/q^n\mathbf Z$. Fix the standard generators $\gamma_i$ of the $\mathbf Z_\ell$ factors. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space with a continuous $E$-linear $G$-action $\rho$. Suppose $Q=\rho(H)$ is finite of order prime to $\ell$. Put $N=M^H=\operatorname{im}(e)$ where $e=|Q|^{-1}\sum_{h\in Q}h$. For $F=E,\Omega$, let $M_F$ be the condensed $C_F$-module $S\mapsto C(S,F\otimes_E M)$, with the finite-dimensional product norm topology on $F\otimes_E M$ and the extended $G$-action; define $N_F$ in the same way from $N$. The category of $G$-equivariant condensed $C_F$-modules means module objects equipped with a $C_F$-linear action of the condensed group $S\mapsto C(S,G)$. Write $R\Gamma_G$ for the ordinary total right derived functor of invariants from this abelian category to condensed $C_F$-modules.

Define a cochain complex $K_F(M)$ in degrees $0,\ldots,r$ by
$$K_F(M)^a=\bigoplus_{|I|=a}N_F,\qquad (dx)_J=\sum_{i\in J}(-1)^{\#\{j\in J:j<i\}}(\rho(\gamma_i)-1)x_{J\setminus\{i\}}.$$
Then there is a natural isomorphism $\kappa_F:K_F(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_G(M_F)$ in the ordinary derived category of condensed $C_F$-modules. The isomorphisms are compatible with the degree-zero inclusion of invariants. For the continuous inclusion $E\to\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], the map $R\Gamma_G(M_E)\to\operatorname{Res}_{C_E\to C_\Omega}R\Gamma_G(M_\Omega)$ induced by $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ corresponds, under $\kappa_E,\kappa_\Omega$, to the termwise inclusion $K_E(M)\to\operatorname{Res}K_\Omega(M)$. If $r=0$, these identifications are the identity $M_F[0]$. Neither a completion nor a union of finite-subextension coefficient sheaves is used.

proof.text: Apply the fixed-summand preparation to $H,L,M$. It gives $N=\operatorname{im}e$, its continuous $L$-action, $(M_F)^H=N_F$, and the prime-to-$\ell$ property of every finite quotient of $H$. The reduction therefore applies with $B=H,V=M$ and gives $a_F:R\Gamma_L(N_F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_G(M_F)$, with its naturality, invariant normalization and coefficient square.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-boundary input below the open-coefficient preservation assertion; repaired assembly step 1

proof.text: Apply dense-lattice restriction with $V=N$, $D=\mathbf Z^r$ and $\iota(e_i)=\gamma_i$. This gives $b_F:R\Gamma_L(N_F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_D(\operatorname{Res}_\iota N_F)$. Apply the strict model construction with $A_i=\rho(\gamma_i)|_N-1$. The operators commute; its coordinates, differential and literal coefficient inclusions are those of $K_F(M)$. The discrete Koszul resolution, with $R=C_F$ and $P=\operatorname{Res}_\iota N_F$, then gives $\lambda_F:K_F(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_D(\operatorname{Res}_\iota N_F)$, with exactly the alternating deletion sign.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-boundary input below the open-coefficient preservation assertion; repaired assembly step 2

proof.text: Define $\kappa_F=a_Fb_F^{-1}\lambda_F$. Composing naturality squares, with that for $b_F$ inverted, proves naturality. On invariant elements, $\lambda_F$ is the degree-zero inclusion, $b_F$ is the identity under the invariant identification, and $a_F$ comes from $N_F\hookrightarrow M_F$; hence the composite has the prescribed invariant normalization.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-boundary input below the open-coefficient preservation assertion; repaired assembly step 3

proof.text: Let $u_A,u_B,u_C$ be the coefficient maps on the $G,L,D$ derived invariants, and $u_K$ the literal subset-coordinate map supplied by the strict model. The three coefficient clauses give $u_Aa_E=(\operatorname{Res}a_\Omega)u_B$, $u_Cb_E=(\operatorname{Res}b_\Omega)u_B$ and $u_C\lambda_E=(\operatorname{Res}\lambda_\Omega)u_K$. Inverting the middle square gives $u_Bb_E^{-1}=(\operatorname{Res}b_\Omega)^{-1}u_C$. Substitution yields $u_A\kappa_E=(\operatorname{Res}\kappa_\Omega)u_K$, the required coefficient comparison. Here $u_K$ sends $x_I$ to $1\otimes x_I$, with every differential matrix over $E$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-boundary input below the open-coefficient preservation assertion; repaired assembly step 4

proof.text: For $r=0$ the preparation gives $H=L=D=1$, $Q=1$, $e=1$ and $N=M$. The trivial-factor, rank-zero restriction and rank-zero Koszul normalizations make all three factors identities, so $\kappa_F=1_{M_F[0]}$. If $M=0$ or $N=0$, the strict model is zero and the comparison is its unique isomorphism. Every object throughout uses all continuous norm-topological sections, without completion or a union of coefficient fields.
